title: blurb
Steam diffusion over seventeen centuries: From Hero’s spinning toy to Watt’s machines — almost two millennia where the physics of gas and vacuum had to become thinkable, demonstrable, and paid for before “railroad time.”

title: coal-mining
Steam diffusion over seventeen centuries: Hero proved sealed vapor can spin; coal is the long fuse—dense fuel stockpiled centuries before anyone earns a living optimizing a cylinder against it.

title: hydrostatics
Steam diffusion over seventeen centuries: Pits go where wood no longer reaches; lift limits turn into daily accounts—pressure as stacked geometry in liquids is the vocabulary later borrowed for air.

title: gas
Steam diffusion over seventeen centuries: Once water columns behave predictably, the sloppier lumping of every vapor as generic “air” becomes the next debt—distinct gases make experiments composable.

title: barometer
Steam diffusion over seventeen centuries: Classification meets a paying puzzle: lift pumps stalled at ~33 ft, so atmospheric weight stops being philosophy and becomes a number on a ruler.

title: air-pump
Steam diffusion over seventeen centuries: Torricelli measured the void; Guericke’s seals make it something you can manufacture, break, and repair—repeatable craft instead of one-off glassware luck.

title: air-pressure
Steam diffusion over seventeen centuries: Bench curiosity scales to theater: when teams of horses can’t pull hemispheres apart, sponsors—not just natural philosophers—see that vacuum does macroscopic work.

title: boyles-law
Steam diffusion over seventeen centuries: Public proofs of air’s strength invite the boring next step: squeeze the spring in a controlled way until volume and pressure trade off as a design rule.

title: pressure-cooker
Steam diffusion over seventeen centuries: Boyle hands designers a compressible rule; Papin bolts it onto Hero’s sealed-kettle intuition—the first sealed steam that earns dinner, not tenure.

title: miners-friend
Steam diffusion over seventeen centuries: Credible small boilers meet the customer who cannot refuse a bad pump—flooded English collieries pay for Savery’s violent shortcut because the fuel base is already coal.

title: gas-volume-temperature
Steam diffusion over seventeen centuries: A year later, still burning coal to argue with gravity, Amontons adds temperature to the gas-law family—another scalar for anyone who will soon count duty per bushel.

title: newcomen-steam-engine
Steam diffusion over seventeen centuries: Amontons finishes the ‘gas plus heat’ picture on the bench; the paying problem is still the flooded seam—Newcomen trades Savery’s high-pressure terror for a slower beat collieries will actually run underground.

title: latent-heat
Steam diffusion over seventeen centuries: Terrible duty per bushel makes “missing” heat in phase changes economically visible—Black gives accountants a place for heat that does not register on a thermometer yet.

title: steam-engine
Steam diffusion over seventeen centuries: Watt’s repair assignment applies that bookkeeping to geometry: always-hot versus always-cold space is how latent heat stops being wasted motion in the cylinder.

title: improved-steam-engine
Steam diffusion over seventeen centuries: Rotary output and steadier pressure fold the toy line into mills—the same fire that once entertained courts now signs factory ledgers.
